lines.say: Volume is the amount of space inside a solid.
A prism has the same cross-section all the way along.
Think of a loaf of sliced bread. Every slice is the same shape.

frames.heading: Area of the end times length

lines.say: Start with one slice. Its area is A.
Stack identical slices all along the length.

draw.alt: Identical slices stacked along the length

lines.say: So the volume is the area of the end times the length.
lines.alt: Prism with end face area A and length along the side

lines.say: The length is measured at right angles to the cross-section.
This end is a trapezium. Parallel sides 4 and 10, height 5.
lines.alt: Prism 20 cm long with trapezium end: parallel sides 4 cm and 10 cm, height 5 cm

lines.say: Area is a half times 4 plus 10, times 5. That's 35.
The trapezium repeats for 20 centimetres.
A cylinder's cross-section is a circle, area pi r squared.
A can has radius 3 and height 8. Square the radius only.
lines.alt: Cylinder with radius r and height h

lines.say: 72 pi is about 226.2 cubic centimetres. That's 226.2 millilitres.
If you're given the diameter, halve it first. Halve it, square it, pi it, height it.
Capacity is how much a container holds.
A 10 centimetre cube holds exactly 1 litre.
A cubic metre holds 1000 litres.
A tank with radius 1 metre and height 1.5 metres is 1.5 pi cubic metres.
Times 1000. It holds about 4712 litres.
A pipe's end is a ring. Outer radius 5, inner radius 4.

draw.alt: Big circle with the inner hole removed, leaving a ring

lines.say: 25 pi minus 16 pi is 9 pi. Times the length, 100.
To find a missing height, substitute, then solve.
Divide 500 by 25 pi. The height is about 6.37 centimetres.
Don't use the diameter. It gets squared, so the error is times 4.
Use the perpendicular height, not a sloping side.
Change everything to one unit first.
1 cubic metre is 1000 litres, not 100.
Area of the end times length works for every prism.
For a cylinder, pi r squared h.
Volume units always have a cubed.
